---
emoji: "🧹"
description: Closes ephemeral AI-generated daily/weekly report discussions older than 14 days to keep the discussions corpus clean and navigable
on:
  schedule: daily
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  discussions: read

sandbox:
  agent:
    sudo: false

engine:
  id: copilot
  copilot-sdk: true
strict: true
tracker-id: discussion-janitor
timeout-minutes: 10

tools:
  bash:
    - "jq *"
    - "cat *"
    - "date *"

steps:
  - name: Fetch stale AI report discussions
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_AW_GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN || secrets.GH_AW_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    run: |
      mkdir -p /tmp/gh-aw/agent

      # Calculate cutoff date (14 days ago) - supports both GNU and BSD date
      CUTOFF=$(date -d '14 days ago' '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' 2>/dev/null || date -v-14d '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
      echo "Cutoff date: $CUTOFF"

      # Fetch open discussions via GraphQL (up to 100 per page, two pages max)
      DISCUSSIONS_FILE="/tmp/gh-aw/agent/all-discussions.json"
      echo '[]' > "$DISCUSSIONS_FILE"

      CURSOR=""
      for PAGE in 1 2; do
        if [ -z "$CURSOR" ]; then
          AFTER_ARG=""
        else
          AFTER_ARG=", after: \"$CURSOR\""
        fi

        RESULT=$(gh api graphql -f query="
          query {
            repository(owner: \"github\", name: \"gh-aw\") {
              discussions(first: 100, states: [OPEN]${AFTER_ARG}, orderBy: {field: CREATED_AT, direction: ASC}) {
                pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
                nodes {
                  number
                  title
                  createdAt
                  body
                  category { slug }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        ")

        HAS_NEXT=$(echo "$RESULT" | jq -r '.data.repository.discussions.pageInfo.hasNextPage')
        CURSOR=$(echo "$RESULT" | jq -r '.data.repository.discussions.pageInfo.endCursor // empty')

        # Append nodes to accumulated file
        echo "$RESULT" | jq \
          --arg cutoff "$CUTOFF" \
          '[
            .data.repository.discussions.nodes[]
            | select(
                .createdAt < $cutoff
                and (
                  (.category.slug | IN("audits", "reports", "daily-news"))
                  or (.body | test("> AI generated by|> Generated by [^\\n]*(actions/runs|workflow)"; "im"))
                )
                and (.body | test("> AI generated by|> Generated by [^\\n]*(actions/runs|workflow)"; "im"))
              )
            | {number: .number, title: .title, createdAt: .createdAt, category: .category.slug}
          ]' >> "$DISCUSSIONS_FILE.tmp" 2>/dev/null || true

        [ "$HAS_NEXT" = "false" ] && break
      done

      # Merge all pages and limit to 50 per run
      if [ -f "$DISCUSSIONS_FILE.tmp" ]; then
        jq -s 'add | unique_by(.number) | .[0:50]' "$DISCUSSIONS_FILE.tmp" > "$DISCUSSIONS_FILE"
      fi

      COUNT=$(jq 'length' "$DISCUSSIONS_FILE")
      echo "Found $COUNT stale AI report discussions older than 14 days (capped at 50)"
      jq -r '.[] | "  #\(.number): \(.title) (\(.category), \(.createdAt[:10]))"' "$DISCUSSIONS_FILE" || true

safe-outputs:
  close-discussion:
    target: "*"
    max: 50
  noop:
---

# Discussion Janitor

You are a lightweight housekeeping agent. Your sole task is to close ephemeral AI-generated report discussions older than 14 days.

## Context

Daily and weekly AI agent reports (Audits, Daily News, per-agent status) accumulate indefinitely in GitHub Discussions. These ephemeral reports dilute signal for downstream agents and human readers. This workflow cleans them up automatically.

**Protected categories** (never close): Q&A, General, Dev, Announcements, Ideas.
**Target categories**: `audits`, `reports`, `daily-news` — but only when the discussion body contains an `> AI generated by` or `> Generated by` footer marker.

## Task

1. Read `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/all-discussions.json` — this file contains pre-filtered stale discussions (older than 14 days, matching ephemeral report patterns).

2. **If the file is empty or contains `[]`**: call `noop` with the message `"No stale report discussions found — corpus is clean"` and stop.

3. **For each discussion** in the file: output one `close_discussion` JSONL line targeting that discussion number with reason `OUTDATED`. Do not include a body (silence is configured; the closure speaks for itself).

   Example output format:
   ```jsonl
   {"type":"close_discussion","discussion_number":12345,"reason":"OUTDATED"}
   {"type":"close_discussion","discussion_number":12346,"reason":"OUTDATED"}
   ```

4. After emitting all close outputs, call `noop` only if you emitted zero close outputs (i.e., the file was empty).

## Constraints

- Close at most 50 discussions per run (safe-output limit).
- Do not read discussion bodies or comments — use only the pre-fetched data.
- Do not create issues, comments, or any other output — closures only.
- Every run must end with either at least one `close_discussion` output or a `noop` call.

{{#runtime-import shared/noop-reminder.md}}
